what: The heuristic precomputes customer visited/location facts and reconstructs a complete directed routing-cost matrix from grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operator metric costs. At evaluation time it identifies the current location and unvisited customers, computes an MST connectivity relaxation over the current endpoint, remaining customers, and depot, and computes a fast greedy completion route. The returned estimate is 30% MST and 70% greedy completion cost. When exact `capacity()`, customer `demand(...)`, and `load()` PNEs survive translation, the greedy completion inserts capacity-induced depot breaks. Exact vehicle data is also used to recognize proven vehicle-limit dead ends. Missing folded resource PNEs are tolerated, leaving the routing estimate fully operational.
why: CVRP states are principally distinguished by their current route endpoint and remaining customer set, so operator-derived routing costs provide robust, instance-independent guidance without relying on fragile travel-cost PNE names. The MST term captures global geographic connectivity and reduces the myopia of nearest-neighbour routing, while the greedy completion gives a stronger estimate of the actual ordered path and final depot return. Capacity-aware route breaks are valuable on the low-capacity, many-route instances, whereas graceful degradation to an uncapacitated routing estimate is necessary because the translator may eliminate capacity and demand PNEs. The blend is intentionally non-admissible and favors the completion estimate to reduce search expansions.
